newsitem.title: LEBANON: Warning to Beirut not official, pro-Israeli says.
newsitem.headline: Warning to Beirut not official, pro-Israeli says.

text.p: The chief of Israel's proxy militia in south Lebanon said on Friday he was not conveying a message from Israel when he warned Lebanon this week of a possible big Israeli military operation.

General Antoine Lahd of the South Lebanon Army (SLA) said it was his personal analysis when he warned on Wednesday of widescale Israeli retaliation if Moslem guerrillas stepped up raids on Israeli forces occupying a south Lebanon border strip.
"I am not a postman for the Israeli state nor does it need me to get across what it wants to the (Lebanese) government," Lahd told reporters.
The warning had caused concern in Lebanon. Officials said Beirut was taking it seriously and the issue was raised in talks on Thursday between Syria and Lebanon's foreign ministers.

Israel launched a 17-day military attack on Lebanon in April in a failed attempt to crush Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas after tit-for-tat bombardments of civilian areas by the two sides. Some 200 people were killed.
"My statement does not carry any warning, it was an honest personal analysis of the current situation and how matters may end up if they were not handled carefully," Lahd said.
"Things develop quickly and the whole region lives in unstable conditions, which is not hidden from anyone," he added. His 3,000-strong militia helps 1,000 Israeli troops control the border strip.
Lahd issued the warning while urging Lebanon to reconsider Israel's "Lebanon First" proposal for a conditional withdrawal of its troops from south Lebanon.

Israel said in July it was ready to pull out under a deal to be negotiated with Syria, if Syrian troops also left Lebanon and if the Lebanese army could guarantee Israel's security against cross-border guerrilla attacks. Syria and Lebanon rejected the proposal.
